Verdict: KX3 fails, KX1 fails. The mechanics are clean; the headline numbers are not robust.

1. Code and trade-log audit (tax_rotation.ws / tax_rotation.rank): no bug that inflates the result.
- keep-in-top-2N, no-trim, worst-ranked-first gain spending and LT-only all match the label when re-derived independently from instrumented runs (2000-01, 2007-07 and 2015-04 starts).
- Trades go only through ctx.order. Proportional buys never exceed cash, and the engine capped no buy.
- Predicted gains equal engine-booked gains (to 1e-12).
- No wash sale is possible at an S/Q cadence: 0 of 99 loss lots were rebought within +-30 days.
- No look-ahead: with all price data clipped at 2003-02-14, 2012-01-04 and 2020-03-20, every earlier order is identical.
- One deviation, shared with the site's TaxManagedCombo: the budget-limited partial sale is sized as qty*room/gain (the average gain) while the engine sells FIFO lots. The 1% budget was overshot in 18 of 25 years (up to 1.32x).
- Negative cash never occurs in KX3; in KX1 it is rare and below 0.6% of PV.
- Dust: 40% of KX3's trades are top-ups below 0.5% of PV. These are harmless because costs are proportional.

2. Battery, CA:
- Lag 1: score +1.09, full +1.53, boot_p 0.053 (passes).
- Costs (score): 0 bps +1.02, 15 bps +0.96, 35 bps +0.88.
- Stricter tax accounting: +0.03 to +0.06 pp.
- Sub-periods: 2000-10 +2.93, 2010-20 +0.89, 2020-26 -0.40.
- DSR at 12,000 trials: 0.038 (FED 0.048).
- 26 weekly rebalance offsets: score mean +0.94 [+0.65, +1.27], all positive; full mean +1.18 (median +1.00) [+0.48, +2.42]. The default date ranks 3rd of 26 on full_excess. boot_p <= 0.10 at 12/26 offsets; criteria 1-3 pass at 9/26.

3. Exact FIFO budget (the label-faithful fix): the score is unchanged (+0.95), but at the default date full_excess drops from +1.84 to +0.31 and boot_p rises from 0.011 to 0.40.
- The paths split at one 2004 partial sale. The reported path rotated into QQQ in 2009 and ends 2026 with a 46% higher terminal value.
- Averaged over offsets the fix is neutral, so the headline is path luck.

4. Versus the incumbent (same battery):
- Across offsets, KX3's score is better (+0.94 vs +0.61; 10y beat rate 0.88 vs 0.68), but its full-period excess is identical (+1.18 vs +1.18). The incumbent passes criteria 1-3 at 0/13 offsets.
- Paired monthly difference: +0.28 pp/yr, p = 0.38. KX3 is worse in 78% of 20-year windows.

5. Risk: the frozen 2026 books are 56-82% growth/tech, with 76-87% of value as unrealized gain. A replay of the 2000-02 bust loses 56-71% vs SPY -47.5%, and a 1% budget cannot de-risk.

KX1 is weaker across offsets: score mean +0.76, 4/13 pass. DSR 0.051.

verdicts.candidate: KX3: 378-0 momentum, top 5, semiannual, 1% budget, keep-in-top-2N + no-trim + worst-ranked-first gain spending (WS, proportional buys)
reasons: Mechanics are clean. The label semantics re-derive exactly from instrumented trade logs. Trades go only through ctx.order, no buy exceeds cash, predicted gains equal booked gains, there are 0 wash sales (impossible at S cadence), and the data-truncation test shows no look-ahead at 3 cut dates.

The headline full-period result is path luck. Sizing the budget-limited partial sale exactly on FIFO lots (label-faithful) leaves the score at +0.95, but full_excess falls from +1.84 to +0.31 and boot_p rises from 0.011 to 0.40 at the default date. One 2004 partial sale sends the 2000-start path to a QQQ-light book worth 31% less in 2026.

Rebalance timing: over 26 weekly offsets the default date ranks 3rd on full_excess (offset median +1.00). boot_p <= 0.10 at only 12/26 offsets, and criteria 1-3 hold at only 9/26. The score is robust (mean +0.94, all offsets positive).
Deflated Sharpe at 12,000 trials is 0.038 in CA and 0.048 in FED. It is below 0.5 even at 100 effective trials (PSR alone 0.988).

No statistically detectable improvement over the site preset. Paired monthly difference +0.28 pp/yr, p = 0.38. The offset-averaged full_excess is identical (+1.18 vs +1.18). KX3 is worse in 78% of 20-year windows. The 10y beat rate gain (0.88 vs 0.68) is real.

Era: the 2020-26 sub-period is -0.40 pp, and 5y windows starting 2020/2021 lose 3.2 / 4.8 pp/yr. The pre-2000 long-history holdout is negative (full -0.34, ho10 -0.23). The round-1 hindsight failure (QQQ/XLK removal, random menus) stands.

Survives execution realism: lag 1 (CA +1.09 / +1.53, boot 0.053, passes 1-3), costs 0-35 bps (score +1.02 to +0.88), annual-distribution tax (+0.03 to +0.06 pp), skipping trades below 0.5-1% of PV (+1.01).

Untested concentration: the 2026 book is QQQ 33% / XLK 23% (2015-start book: XLK 39% / QQQ 27% / IWF 16%), with 76-87% unrealized gains. A replay of 2000-02 loses 56-71% vs SPY -47.5%, and a 1% budget cannot de-risk.
bugs_found: Budget-limited partial gain sale is sized as qty*room/gain (average gain per share) while the engine realizes FIFO (oldest, lowest-basis lots first). Realized gains overshoot the 1% budget in 18 of 25 years (max 1.32x; e.g. room $1,358 -> realized $2,445 on 2010-01-04). Shared with the site's TaxManagedCombo. Fixed in verify_taxrot_mech.ws_x exact_budget=true; the score is unchanged but the default-date full_excess goes +1.84 -> +0.31.

Not a bug, design note: 'held' in keep-in-top-2N includes residual positions left by budget-limited partial exits, so such a name is kept and topped back up to 1/N while it ranks 6-10 (75 kept-while-ranked-6-10 events over 54 rebalances).

Engine convention, immaterial here: last year's tax is deducted from cash on the first January trading day before the strategy runs, so cash can go negative (interest-free). It never happens for KX3; KX1 2015 start: 371 days, min -0.54% of PV.
Lab note: verify.battery silently skips offsets/lag for custom kinds; verify_taxrot_mech.ws_x provides offset_days/lag for tax_rotation.ws configs.

best_variant_numbers.note: Label-faithful fix (exact FIFO budget), NOT an improvement: these are the honest default-date numbers; the offset-average equals the original's.

summary:
I tried to break KX3 and KX1 on mechanics, bugs and execution realism. Both fail the good-confidence bar, and neither is recommendable as beating SPY after tax with good confidence.

**What held:**
- **The code does what the label says.** Keep-in-top-2N, no-trim, worst-ranked-first gain spending and long-term-only re-derive exactly from instrumented trade logs. Trades go only through ctx.order, buys never exceed cash, and predicted gains equal the gains the engine books.
- **No wash sales and no look-ahead.** A wash sale cannot happen at these rebalance cadences (0 of 99 loss lots rebought within 30 days). Clipping all data at three dates leaves every earlier order identical.
- **The 95-window score is robust to execution.** It survives a 1-day lag, costs up to 35 bps, annual dividend tax, skipping small trades, and all 26 weekly rebalance offsets (KX3 mean +0.94 pp/yr, never below +0.65).

**What broke:**
- **One accounting deviation, shared with the site's TaxManagedCombo.** The last budget-limited sale is sized on the position's average gain, but the engine sells oldest lots first. KX3 overshot its 1% budget in 18 of 25 years.
- **KX3's headline is a lucky path.** Sizing that sale exactly leaves the score unchanged (+0.95) but cuts default-date full_excess from +1.84 to +0.31 and raises boot_p from 0.011 to 0.40. One partial sale in 2004 decides whether the 2000-start book ends 33% QQQ (46% more terminal wealth).
- **The default rebalance date is near the best.** It ranks 3rd of 26 on full_excess; boot_p is at most 0.10 at only 12/26 offsets, and criteria 1-3 pass at 9/26 (KX1: 4/13).
- **Multiple testing:** deflated Sharpe at 12,000 trials is 0.038 for KX3 and 0.051 for KX1.
- **Not detectably better than the incumbent.** The paired difference is +0.28 pp/yr (p = 0.38), and averaged over offsets the full-period excess is identical (+1.18 vs +1.18). The real gain is a higher 10-year beat rate (0.88 vs 0.68).
- **Recent windows and concentration.** The 2020-26 sub-period is negative, and 5-year windows starting 2020/2021 lose 3-5 pp/yr. The frozen 2026 books are 56-82% growth/tech, and replaying the 2000-02 bust on them loses 56-71% vs SPY's -47.5%.

The fixed variants (exact_budget=true in verify_taxrot_mech.ws_x) are label-faithful but not better.
open_questions: Should the site's TaxManagedCombo (and the lab's WeightStrategy/TRStrategy) size the budget-limited partial sale on actual FIFO lots? It overshoots the gain budget by up to ~30% in many years. It is neutral on average, but it changes individual paths a lot (KX3 2000-start full_excess +1.84 vs +0.31).

For path-dependent tax-managed rules, boot_p and full_excess come from a single 2000-start path, which these tests show is chaotic (it swings by about 1 pp/yr under label-faithful accounting changes, cost changes or min-trade changes). Should the protocol's bar 3 use an offset-averaged or multi-start bootstrap instead?
Should verify.battery support offset_days/lag for custom kinds generically (e.g. by wrapping on_day), so that families such as tax_rotation.ws are not silently skipped?

Concentration risk of frozen tax-managed books (56-82% growth/tech, 76-87% unrealized gain, unsellable under a 1% budget) is not captured by historical windows. Should finalists get a forward stress test of their terminal book?
